prompt: Every gang member wears a knitted balaclava covering the whole head, with no eye, nose or mouth holes; a large white ring is stitched round the face, and a red triangle sits high over the wearer's left eye (on the right of the picture, at about 2 o'clock); gloves on both hands, collars and cuffs closed, no skin showing anywhere. The camera rests on the bare concrete floor of a windowless council archive basement, tilted almost straight up through a 14mm rectilinear lens at f/11, so the scuffed floor and a spilled cardboard box fill the bottom of the frame and the verticals rush inward toward the top. Five gang members stand in a loose arc at the base of one towering column of loose A4 paper, so tall it runs out of the top of the portrait frame; their chins are lifted and their masked faces angled upward, in sage, rust, navy, charcoal and mustard knit, wearing a grey hoodie, a black puffer jacket, a hi-vis orange vest over a fleece, a navy work coat and a padded bomber, with work boots and trainers. Long rows of galvanised steel shelving packed with box files close in on both sides like canyon walls. The only light comes from bare fluorescent tubes on the ceiling far above, one of them stuttering, casting a cold greenish white that flattens the clothes into shadow while the stitched white rings and red triangles glow out of the gloom. A plain printed label stuck to the side of the paper column, bold black capitals, reads THE RULES. Everything from the floor grit to the last visible sheet is sharp, so the stack seems to go on forever; documentary realism, fine digital grain, a slight greenish cast in the shadows.
